ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The graph is a titration curve with pH on the y-axis and Volume HCl (mL) on the x-axis. The curve starts at high pH, decreases gradually through the buffer region, then has a sharp vertical drop around about 22–23 mL of HCl, and finally levels off at low pH. The labeled arrows A, B, C, and D point to points before the sharp drop; E points near the steep drop; F points after the equivalence region. Reasoning: For a weak base titrated with a strong acid, pH = pKa of the conjugate acid at the half-equivalence point. The equivalence point is indicated by the sharp drop, roughly near 22 mL of added HCl. Half of that volume is about 11 mL. On the graph, the labeled arrow near 10–11 mL in the gradual buffer region is C.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Uses the quantitative half-equivalence-volume criterion: first locate the equivalence point on the graph, then halve its volume to choose the arrow. This is the standard stoichiometric/Henderson-Hasselbalch route.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the titration curve axes and labeled arrows. Identify the steep vertical drop/inflection as the equivalence region at about 22 mL of added HCl, then locate half of that volume, about 11 mL, where arrow C points on the buffer portion of the curve.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text to know the titration is 25.0 mL of a weak base titrated with 0.125 M HCl and that the requested location is where pH equals the pKa of the conjugate acid.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: For titration of a weak base B with strong acid, before equivalence the buffer contains B and its conjugate acid BH+. At half-equivalence, [B] = [BH+], so Henderson-Hasselbalch for the conjugate acid gives pH = pKa. Therefore the desired point is at one-half the equivalence volume.
